observations.excerpt:
NixlConnector uses NIXL library for underlying communication, which supports multiple transport backends. UCX (Unified Communication X) is the primary default transport library used by NIXL. Configure transport environment variables:

```bash
# Example UCX configuration, adjust according to your environment
export UCX_TLS=all  # or specify specific transports like "rc,ud,sm,^cuda_ipc" ..etc
export UCX_NET_DEVICES=all  # or specify network devices like "mlx5_0:1,mlx5_1:1"
```

!!! tip
    When using UCX as the transport backend, NCCL environment variables (like `NCCL_IB_HCA`, `NCCL_SOCKET_IFNAME`) are not applicable to NixlConnector, so configure UCX-specific environment variables instead of NCCL variables.

#### Selecting a NIXL transport backend (plugin)

NixlConnector can use different NIXL transport backends (plugins). By default, NixlConnector uses UCX as the transport backend.

To select a different backend, set `kv_connector_extra_config.backends` in `--kv-transfer-config`.

### Example: using LIBFABRIC backend

```bash
vllm serve <MODEL> \
  --kv-transfer-config '{
    "kv_connector":"NixlConnector",
    "kv_role":"kv_producer",
    "kv_connector_extra_config":{"backends":["LIBFABRIC"]}
  }'
```

You can also pass JSON keys individually using dotted arguments, and you can append list elements using `+`:

```bash
vllm serve <MODEL> \
  --kv-transfer-config.kv_connector NixlConnector \
  --kv-transfer-config.kv_role kv_producer \
  --kv-transfer-config.kv_connector_extra_config.backends+ LIBFABRIC
```

!!! note
    Backend availability depends on how NIXL was built and what plugins are present in your environment. Refer to the [NIXL repository](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/nixl) for available backends and build instructions.

#### UCX backend parameters

`kv_connector_extra_config.ucx_backend_params` passes extra init parameters to NIXL's UCX backend. Values are strings. For example, NIXL creates UCX with `ucx_error_handling_mode=peer` by default; UCX then uses only transports that can detect peer failure, which can exclude intra-node GPU transports such as `rocm_ipc`. Enable bidirectional KV transfer by setting `bidirectional_kv_xfer` in `kv_connector_extra_config` on **both** P and D instances:

```bash
# Prefill instance
vllm serve <MODEL> \
  --kv-transfer-config '{
    "kv_connector": "NixlConnector",
    "kv_role": "kv_producer",
    "kv_connector_extra_config": {
      "bidirectional_kv_xfer": true
    }
  }'

# Decode instance
vllm serve <MODEL> \
  --kv-transfer-config '{
    "kv_connector": "NixlConnector",
    "kv_role": "kv_consumer",
    "kv_connector_extra_config": {
      "bidirectional_kv_xfer": true
    }
  }'
```

Additional configuration options in `kv_connector_extra_config`:

| Parameter | Default | Description |
| --------- | ------- | ----------- |
| `bidirectional_kv_xfer` | `false` | Enable bidirectional D→P KV transfer. |
| `kv_recompute_threshold` | `64` | Minimum number of remote tokens required to trigger a D→P pull. Below this threshold, P recomputes locally instead of pulling (to amortize transfer latency). |
| `decoder_kv_blocks_ttl` | `480` | TTL (seconds) for KV blocks cached on D for bidirectional reuse. Blocks are released after this duration. Not renewed via heartbeats. |

observations.excerpt:
## Decode allocation policy

By default, decode reserves each request's destination KV slots before prefill
finishes. Long prefills can hold these slots while decode waits for the KV data.
To delay this reservation, set the following flag on **both prefill and decode**:

```bash
--disaggregation-decode-allocation-policy prefill_complete
```

With `prefill_complete`, prefill computes without waiting for destination slots,
then signals readiness after accepting its final prefill result. Decode reserves
slots and starts the existing KV transfer handshake only after that signal.
This changes per-request KV reservation, not the size or creation of the global
KV pool. The default `early` policy preserves the existing behavior.

Deferring allocation can help when long prefills compete with active decode
requests for destination KV capacity. It also retains KV on prefill longer and
removes overlap between chunked prefill and KV transfer. Compare both policies
for your workload; this option is not a general throughput improvement.

This initial implementation requires Mooncake (RDMA or `mooncake_tcp`), the Python
bootstrap registry, and attention TP/CP and pipeline sizes of one. Attention DP
is allowed when each DP rank has attention TP size one. Prefill automatically
resolves `--optimistic-prefill-attempts` from zero to one; configurations that
disable optimistic prefill after model validation are rejected.
Chunked prefill does not yield just because decode has not admitted the request.
Completed requests retain their KV in the existing optimistic-prefill inflight
queue until decode supplies destination indices; readiness alone never starts
a KV write.
After a successful transfer, prefill clears the room's readiness and transfer
state before notifying decode of success. Retraction recovery can then reuse
the same bootstrap room. This notification waits for worker and scheduler
cleanup; failure and cancellation records remain until their timeout expires.
Retries remain eligible for prefill after the optimistic attempt budget is
exhausted and remain subject to the existing cancellation and timeout handling.

On prefill, `SGLANG_DISAGGREGATION_BOOTSTRAP_TIMEOUT` starts after the final
prefill result, giving decode admission its own budget. On decode,
`SGLANG_DISAGGREGATION_WAITING_TIMEOUT` bounds the wait for prefill completion,
then starts afresh for admission and again when destination indices are sent
for transfer.

The option does not support staging buffers, runtime PD role switching,
encoder disaggregation, decoupled speculation, HiSparse, decode radix cache, decode
HiCache, or non-DSA auxiliary state pools. Prefill HiCache is limited to L2 with
`write_back` and no storage backend. Unsupported configurations fail validation.

All communicating workers must use the same revision and enable the same policy. This
version of the decode worker rejects policy or peer-layout mismatches before
destination registration. Older decode workers do not enforce this check. Keep
`early` on both sides until every worker has been upgraded, then enable the new
policy on both sides.

observations.interpretation: Current documented precedence: explicit backend device_list overrides UCX_NET_DEVICES; nonempty UCX_NET_DEVICES bypasses disaggregation-ib-device, including per-GPU CLI mappings.
observations.excerpt:
#### UCX device selection

For NVIDIA CUDA and AMD ROCm deployments using NIXL UCX, `--disaggregation-ib-device` accepts a shared HCA list or a per-GPU JSON/file mapping. Mapping keys are process-visible GPU IDs; use HCA names without port suffixes, such as `mlx5_0`.

A non-empty `UCX_NET_DEVICES` takes precedence over this CLI option. SGLang leaves the environment variable unchanged and skips the CLI mapping, including per-GPU mappings, with a warning. This preserves interfaces such as `lo` in an existing configuration like `rdma0:1,rdma4:1,lo`, which some RoCE hosts need for NIXL's self-endpoint.

To use per-GPU CLI selection, unset `UCX_NET_DEVICES`; keep it configured on hosts that require the loopback entry. An explicit `device_list` in `SGLANG_DISAGGREGATION_NIXL_BACKEND_PARAMS` is left unchanged and still overrides `UCX_NET_DEVICES`; do not set it if you rely on the environment's complete device list.

### Prefill/Decode Disaggregation (PD)
- **Rust binary**
  ```bash
  ./target/release/sgl-model-gateway \
    --pd-disaggregation \
    --prefill http://prefill1:30001 9001 \
    --prefill http://prefill2:30002 \

    --policy cache_aware \

observations.interpretation: Cache-aware routing has cache/load thresholds; power_of_two uses observed worker load. The cache-aware tree is router metadata, not the engine KV eviction policy.
observations.excerpt:
## Load Balancing Policies
- `random`: uniform random worker selection.
- `round_robin`: sequential rotation with atomic counters.
- `cache_aware`: maintains a prefix tree of prompts to route repeat traffic and evens load with configurable thresholds (`--cache-threshold`, `--balance-abs-threshold`, `--balance-rel-threshold`, `--eviction-interval`, `--max-tree-size`).
- `power_of_two`: chooses the lighter worker among two random candidates; integrates with `LoadMonitor`.
  Per-model overrides are available in PD mode (`--prefill-policy`, `--decode-policy`) and IGW mode via the worker registry.

observations.interpretation: Native runtime role switching requires an idle instance; rebuild failure is fatal and has no in-place rollback.
The role-switch handler rejects active work and checks headroom before a first decode graph capture. It does not migrate in-flight requests.
A switch rebuilds role-specific structures; rebuild failure marks the instance unhealthy. Decode graphs are prepared when required.
The feature must be enabled, the backend must support it, and staging buffers are excluded.

observations.interpretation: The native preparation mode checks readiness without teardown. Idle/headroom constraints still apply.

For multiple DP workers, readiness is checked across all workers before executing a role switch. The caller must drain ingress and serialize changes. This is not a general policy transaction or live migration protocol.
observations.excerpt:
async def pd_role_switch(
        self: TokenizerManager,
        obj: PdRoleSwitchReqInput,
        request: Optional[fastapi.Request] = None,
    ) -> PdRoleSwitchReqOutput:
        self.auto_create_handle_loop()
        if not self.server_args.enable_pd_role_switch:
            return PdRoleSwitchReqOutput(
                success=False,
                message="--enable-pd-role-switch is not set on this server",
                old_role=get_disagg().disaggregation_mode,
                new_role=obj.new_role,
                safe_to_restore=True,
            )
        # The caller must drain ingress and serialize role-switch requests.
        # Check every DP worker before allowing any of them to tear down.
        if get_parallel().num_dp_ranks > 1:
            prepare_req = copy.copy(obj)
            prepare_req.prepare_only = True
            results = await self.pd_role_switch_communicator(prepare_req)
            if results and all(r.success for r in results) and not obj.prepare_only:
                results = await self.pd_role_switch_communicator(obj)
        else:
            results = await self.pd_role_switch_communicator(obj)
        all_success = bool(results) and all(r.success for r in results)
        safe_to_restore = bool(results) and all(r.safe_to_restore for r in results)
        if all_success and not obj.prepare_only:
            # Keep the tokenizer-manager's view of the role in sync so future
            # control ops and bootstrap routing behave consistently.
            self.record_config_updates(
                "tokenizer.pd_role_switch", disaggregation_mode=obj.new_role
            )
            self.disaggregation_mode = DisaggregationMode(obj.new_role)
            msg = "ok"
        elif all_success:
            msg = "ready"
        else:
            # Surface only the failing workers' messages.
            msg = "; ".join(r.message for r in results if not r.success)
        return PdRoleSwitchReqOutput(
            success=all_success,
            message=msg,
            old_role=results[0].old_role if results else "",
            new_role=obj.new_role,
            safe_to_restore=safe_to_restore,
        )

observations.interpretation: A nonempty UCX_NET_DEVICES skips the CLI HCA mapping. Without it, conflicting explicit backend device_list and CLI selections are rejected.

version_changes: The first scheduler action consumers and SGLang internal-state allowlist retain their prior semantics.
SGLang adds prefill_decode_interval_min_bs and preserves no-decode/DP cadence distinctions.
SGLang NIXL documents and implements HCA mapping and UCX environment/backend-parameter precedence.
SGLang role switching adds prepare_only readiness checks across DP workers; target draining and failure constraints remain.
vLLM NIXL is now included in this audit: initialization controls, bidirectional reuse threshold, D TTL, and P lease state are examined separately from proposed live controls.

The action schema, policy versions, online tuning controller, transfer admission budgets and their end-to-end evaluation remain proposed work.
Role switching and general hot-policy updates have different continuity contracts.
NIXL findings apply to the audited paths and do not establish identical capabilities across all vLLM connectors.
